motivation_from_local_measurements.caution: Historical variable-input medians are not paired with this new fixed study. They motivate investigation, not a speed ratio.

local_source_observation: The existing precision-repair INT8 MMA forms a new integer partial sum for each K128 weight group, converts it to FP32, rescales and accumulates. Activations use per-token maxabs in W4A8. Merely selecting INT8 MMA has not produced fast prefill in this implementation.
hypothesis: In a fresh isolated candidate, retain original W4A16 decode and original checkpoints on disk. At startup expand the FP16-dequantized W4 projection weights into per-output-channel INT8 weights for prefill. Per-token INT8 activations and one whole-K integer GEMM can move floating scaling to the epilogue. Measure the full activation-quantization/GEMM/epilogue cost and extra resident memory.
semantic_boundary: This intentionally introduces a second quantization of prefill weights and quantizes prefill activations. It is a new arithmetic/precision recipe, not an equivalent W4A16 execution optimization and not a direct reproduction of QQQ or QServe. Keep results separate from the unchanged-weight system study.
required_before_adoption: Independent packed-weight/dequantization reference, finite and repeatable numerical results on actual layers and shapes
Compare numerical error with the intended new INT8 arithmetic and separately measure approximation error versus the original dequantized weights
Time activation quantization, padding if required, integer GEMM and output rescaling together; report startup conversion separately
Measure complete-model peak memory and HTTP with equally optimized FP16 and native AWQ controls
Original-policy closed-loop quality cohort, separately reported; no accuracy-equivalence assumption from microbenchmarks

primary_sources.finding: QServe explains how weight or partial-sum dequantization inside the GEMM main loop can limit low-bit performance. Its progressive quantization is designed to reduce that overhead. Whole-K W8A8 applies its scale in the epilogue.
primary_sources.limitation: Its serving-throughput and roofline results are for different hardware, models and workloads; no corresponding speedup is predicted for this RTX4070Ti navigation workload. Its quantization format cannot be assumed compatible with our existing asymmetric packed weights.

primary_sources.finding: QQQ targets both prefill and decode with W4A8 plus smoothing, Hessian-based compensation and specialized kernels. The abstract reports up to2.24x versus FP16 and1.25x versus W4A16.
primary_sources.limitation: These are paper results, not this project's results or a promise. The identity of the paper previously shown to the user remains unconfirmed.
primary_sources.reported_speedup_context: Section4.3 same-batch throughput, LLaMA-2-13B on A10080GB, vLLM0.4.1/PyTorch2.1.2/CUDA11.8, continuous batching and paged attention, input1024/output128. Small batches have comparable speed to W4A16; gain grows with batch size.
primary_sources.compatibility: Section3.3 explicitly restricts QQQ kernels to symmetric weight quantization. Current project packed weights are asymmetric; no drop-in compatibility claim.
